::: {#thm-chi-square-null}
#### Large-sample null distribution of the chi-square statistic

Let $n$ observations be sampled independently
and classified by two categorical variables,
and let the two variables be independent.
Then as $n \to \infty$,
the distribution of $X^2$ (@def-chi-square-test)
converges to the $\chi^2_{(r-1)(c-1)}$ distribution
[@hoggtanis2015, Section 9.2, p. 440].
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#rem-expected-count-rule}
#### Small expected counts

The chi-square approximation is poor when some expected counts are small.
A common rule of thumb asks for every $E_{ij}$ to be at least 5.
:::
